title: This Fish Lays Its Eggs Out of the Water, Then Splashes Them for 3 Days
subject: splash tetra fish

scenes.text: A fish that lays its eggs where fish can't live.
The splash tetra, shorter than your finger, from the Amazon. The pair leaps out of the water together and clings under a leaf.
In a second they stick a few eggs there, drop back, and jump again. Up to two hundred eggs, centimetres above the river.
Up there, nothing in the water can eat them. But in minutes, they would dry out.
So the male stays below and flicks water at them with his tail, about once a minute, for two to three days.
When the fry hatch, they drop straight into the river. Born in the air, kept alive by a splash.

description:
The splash tetra lays its eggs out of the water: the pair leaps together and glues them to the underside of a leaf a few centimetres above the surface.
The eggs are safe from aquatic predators but would dry out, so the male stays beneath and splashes them with his tail roughly every minute for two to three days until the fry hatch and fall into the water. A female can lay up to about 200 eggs this way.
Which animal parent works the hardest?
tags: fish lays eggs out of water
first_comment: If the male stops splashing for an hour, the whole clutch dies. Which fish behaviour has surprised you most?
